explanation: Remove the last character and recursively permute the preceding substring. Insert that removed character at every position in each smaller permutation, storing results in an ordered std::set.
correctness: Deleting one occurrence of the last character from any full permutation leaves a permutation of the shorter input, which recursion produces. Reinserting it at every position therefore reconstructs every result; the ordered set removes duplicates.
walkthrough: For ab, recurse on a to obtain {a}. Insert the removed last character b at position 0 to get ba and at position 1 to get ab. The ordered set contains {ab,ba}. For empty input return {""}, allowing the first nonempty recursion level to insert its character. Return a set of strings; the adapter displays a JSON array and compares membership without imposing output order.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
Empty input returns the singleton set {""}; repeated characters yield distinct strings only, not repeated output entries.
timeComplexity: O(n*n!*log(n!+1)) worst-case time for distinct characters: n! candidate strings cost O(n) to copy/insert characters, and each ordered-set insertion can make O(log(n!+1)) lexicographic comparisons costing O(n). This includes the ordered-set cost, unlike a hash-set bound.
spaceComplexity: O(n*n!) worst-case result and intermediate string storage, plus recursion depth O(n); repeated characters can reduce the number of distinct results.
